examples.text: Counterfeit sad looks, / Make mouths upon me when I turn my back.

glosses: To speak; to utter.

examples.text: He mouthed his opinions on the subject at the meeting.
mouthing big phrases

glosses: To represent (words or sounds) by making the actions of speech, but silently, without producing sound; to frame.

examples.text: The prompter mouthed the words to the actor, who had forgotten them.
One was of a face repeatedly mouthing the vowel sound eee, the other was of a face repeatedly mouthing the vowel sound ahhh.
It should be explained that lip patterns are generally not the same as patterns which would be made by 'mouthing' words.

glosses: To move the mouth, with or without sound; to form (air or words) with the mouth, with or without sound.

examples.text: But words are nothing to the misbelieving -- mere air mouthed into a sound.

There was also a close temporal contiguity between "smiling" or other "emotional" grimaces and mouthing and tonguing movements, so that it was often difficult to distinguish between mouthing and smiling.

glosses: To utter with a voice that is overly loud or swelling.

examples.text: Those who endeavor to become eloquent by mere imitation of some celebrated model—an actor for instance—often attempt to gain this quality by altering their voice in an unnatural manner. Such a process never produces any thing but mouthing.
This view of voice cultivation excludes all mouthing and ranting which have been thought to be necessary incidents of voice culture.

glosses: To exit at a mouth (such as a river mouth)

examples.text: In this part of the address the position of the principal hanging-valleys was indicated , and it was pointed out that there were two sets, namely those which mouthed into valleys that had been deepened in softer rocks, and those which mouthed into portions of main valleys that had been deepened along shatter-bolts.

Suddenly an avalanche of stones turned loose right down a ravine and mouthed out on the road, stones large enough to knock a horse down, or larger, and a plenty of them to do a fair job on a large group.

glosses: To pick up or handle with the lips or mouth, but not chew or swallow.

examples.text: He would not touch any of our food that the bears had pawed and mouthed over, fearing it might be bad medicine for him, so some was got for him from Red Wing Woman.
The fish mouthed the lure, but didn't bite.

Everyone is kind of aroused, Thanatz is sitting up on the bar having his own as yet unsheathed penis mouthed by one of the white-gloved Wends.
She found foamy saliva where the coyote had mouthed over the dogs, but no place showed any bite.

glosses: To take into the mouth; to seize or grind with the mouth or teeth; to chew; to devour.

examples.text: Sometimes I ate food that the rats had already mouthed over; picking away the edges where they had been eating and using the remainder; not with any good grace, not without qualms; but because I had nothing else to eat.
Each contained a long, wide, solid oak table around which all who could find a space the width of his body would mouth his brown-bag grub from home.

glosses: To form or cleanse with the mouth; to lick, as a bear licks her cub.

examples.text: They were sucking off whatever adhered to the floating stems and leaves of the plants. They went from plant to plant and mouthed over each branch from base to tip until the whole plant had been gone over.

glosses: To carry in the mouth.

glosses: To make mouths at

examples.text: He drew the cork from his bottle..and mouthed at his companions even while he bowed to them.

glosses: To form a mouth or opening in.

examples.text: The front end of the barrel has to be mouthed out conically, so that the various centre points may fit it.

glosses: To examine the teeth of.

examples.text: Either at the shipping point or as they leave the summer range, the older ewes are “mouthed out.” That is, their mouths are examined to see if their teeth are good for another year.
